messages:
kerry: started driver 538 rollout to H100 canary (us-west-2). first canary jobs are failing, filing here so infra + runtime can triage

deploy-bot: driver-upgrade: started rollout to pool=h100-canary-usw2 at 2026-04-05T14:20:31Z

alex: what errors are we seeing? can you paste logs?

kerry: paste from one of the failing containers:
```
[FlashAttention] ptx compile error: ptxas fatal   : Unrecognized option '--gpu-name sm_90'
tensorrt: failed to create plugin instance: unresolved symbol: __nv*some_symbol
xformers_cuda: ptx assembly failed for kernel=queryK: ptxas exited with code 1
NCCL WARN Call failed: unhandled cuda error (77) on rank 2
```

rachel: this is only on the h100-canary pool in us-west-2 so far. a100 pools in the same region look fine (no flashattn errors).

josh: saw something similar in eu-central earlier today with TRT 8.7 + CUDA 538 — xformers kernels hit ptx/compat issues when toolchain expects older ptx version. TRT plugin load failing too.

maya: immediate plan: pause the rollout, rollback canary to 535, and cordon/drain the 538 nodes in canary. pressure on capacity but safer.

infra-bot: canary-summary: nodes_total=12 nodes_failed=5 pods_failed=34 failed_jobs=7

kerry: rolling back canary driver -> scheduling rollback job now (do not reboot nodes in the canary group until rollback confirms).

alex: if we push workloads to CPU as fallback be aware the cost hit is large — last CPU fallback run for a similar job spiked cost ~6x for that namespace. need budget signoff if prolonged.

maya: checklist for triage (please attach to this thread): nvcc --version, nvidia-smi output, dmesg, the failing container's torch/torch_cuda build info, TRT and flashattn build flags. Also whether kernels were precompiled vs JITed.

josh: quick mitigation idea: for user hermetic builds we can try forcing PTX target back to sm_80 during flashattn/xformers wheel build (recompile libs) but that's slow and risky in prod. Better to get driver rollback + vendor ticket.

kerry: opened support ticket with NVIDIA (case 2026-INV-9982). Included sample kernel failures and container logs.

rachel: note: some teams in other regions are blocked on lower-latency features that rely on flashattn. if rollback takes >2h, we may need to route those jobs to dedicated reserved A100 capacity temporarily. ops, pls estimate swap latency.

infra-bot: ticket-tracker: https://redwood.internal/tickets/2026-INV-9982 (added logs and failing node ids)

alex: FYI — telemetry shows a small spike in prefix cache misses after the rollback window while nodes reschedule. nothing major but call it out for observability folks.

maya: followups: 1) hold all driver rollouts until vendor confirms compatibility; 2) sweep canary images for precompiled PTX artifacts; 3) run a small TRT 8.8 vs 8.7 matrix on a staging H100 with CUDA 538 to isolate whether TRT or driver is the main culprit.

kerry: holding rollout. re-running smoke with pinned TRT 8.7 on one canary node to reproduce. will post logs here.

josh: when you have a failing container, also run `strings /usr/local/lib/libtorch_cuda.so | grep ptx` — that often shows embedded ptx versions and helps root cause quickly.

kerry: thanks all — rolling back now, keeping the canary cordoned. will update once rollback completes (ETA ~15m). :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: driver-upgrade: rollback initiated for pool=h100-canary-usw2 at 2026-04-05T14:35:12Z

kerry: rollback finished, canary nodes back on 535, failures cleared in canary. pausing all driver batches until NVIDIA responds.

alex: noted. I'll open a cost alert for any prolonged CPU fallbacks and ping product owners.

maya: filing a short postmortem draft with root-cause hypothesis (ptx version mismatch between new driver toolchain and precompiled kernels) and mitigation steps (hold rollouts, recompile wheels with target sm_90, expand canary coverage for TRT/xformers combos).

rachel: good catch — thanks for quick rollback.

josh: thanks — keep me posted on vendor reply and any patches we can test in staging.

kerry: will follow up in this thread when vendor responds. ending thread for now.
